subject.title: Bound historical public repository proof reuse after expiry

question: Does the documented five-second historical-proof allowance remain the intended authorization policy, and does current main enforce it identically in runtime validation and the authoritative D1 query?
rationale: The requested behavior affects whether expired public-visibility evidence may authorize cached content during GitHub failures; documentation alone is insufficient to confirm the intended and implemented security boundary.

options.title: Verify and resolve as implemented
options.body: Confirm the runtime guard, D1 query, and boundary tests all enforce the documented five-second allowance, then close with the proving commit and release/main provenance.

options.title: Land a narrow repair
options.body: If either enforcement point lacks the bound, restore the same policy in both locations with inside-window and beyond-window regression coverage.

recommendation.title: Verify and resolve as implemented
recommendation.body: Confirm the runtime guard, D1 query, and boundary tests all enforce the documented five-second allowance, then close with the proving commit and release/main provenance.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior public-proof fallback history and adjacent merged relay/security work make steipete the strongest available routing candidate.
